note: Second review of the C12-early work (wf_a43c3d53-c25), stopped by a container restart before its third reviewer, fix and verify ran. Findings are unverified by a fix agent.

findings.issue: The room save request skips jupyter-collaboration's own 'never save' setting. With `--YDocExtension.document_save_delay=None` (documented upstream as 'the document will never be saved'), `_maybe_save_document(save_now=True)` still saves. So every nh write and every run end now writes the .ipynb, including the user's unsaved edits in the room. Before this change nothing was written. This contradicts the side doc (docs/plans/c12-design-6.13.md line 122): 'the room already autosaved whenever nh was connected; an explicit save changes when, not whether'. That holds for the client-side autosave flag, not for the server's save delay.
findings.evidence: Upstream code: jupyter_server_ydoc/rooms.py `_maybe_save_document`: `if self._save_delay is None and not save_now: return`. `_save_to_disc` (the RAW 'save' handler) passes save_now=True. app.py help text: 'Defaults to 1s, if None then the document will never be saved.' I probed this in scratch copies (c12b/review-gateway/p-repo, p-m1): conftest was changed to start Lab with only `--YDocExtension.document_save_delay=None`, then `backend.insert_cells(ref, -1, [NewCell(id='c1', ...)])`, then a 4 s wait and a read of the .ipynb. With the fix the disk held ['title', 'c1'] and the lab log showed 'Saving the content from room ...' twice. With the mutant that has no save calls (m1) the disk held ['title'].
findings.fix: At least correct side doc line 122 and add a known gap: 'with document_save_delay=None the room never autosaves, but nh's save requests still write the file (user edits included)'. nh can't read the server's save delay from the client. If this should be honoured, the only option is a harness.toml opt-out; otherwise document it.

findings.issue: `save()` orders the request after the write's update only by `settle()` (two `sleep(0)`). `request_save()` sends directly on the websocket, while nbmodel sends doc updates from its own queue in a sender task. Under websocket backpressure (sender paused in `drain()`), a queued update (e.g. end_run's after the final flush, or an insert queued behind a large output flush) is still in the queue when the save bytes are written. The save then goes first, and the room saves without the write. Also, `await websocket.send()` waits in `drain()` while the transport is paused, so insert/update/delete/set_meta tool calls can now wait on the network. `settle()` never did; the wait ends only when the socket drains or websockets' keepalive closes it (defaults 20 s + 20 s). The known gap (side doc line 166: '...the next save or autosave has it') also understates the impact: while another cell streams, autosave never fires, so the write reaches disk only at nh's next write or run end. That is the a8 root cause.
findings.evidence: Code: jupyter_nbmodel_client/client.py `_send_messages` awaits `websocket.send` per queued message. websockets/asyncio/connection.py `send_context` runs `self.send_data(); await self.drain()` (line ~915), and `drain` waits while `self.paused`. rtc.py:78 `request_save` calls `websocket.send` directly. Ordering matters: a scratch mutant with the settle() before the request removed (c12b/review-gateway/m4) fails all 3 a8 tests (both restart variants lose cells; the streaming root-cause test times out). tests/unit/test_rtc_save.py still passes 5/5 on that mutant, so only integration pins the ordering. I could NOT reproduce backpressure on this machine: a local room server whose event loop was blocked for 12 s still had 10 MB and 60 MB writes accepted with `transport.get_write_buffer_size() == 0`, `paused False`, even with SO_RCVBUF 64 KiB on the listening socket, and the server read [update, update, RAW save] in order (scripts order_demo.py/order_demo2.py). So the race is PLAUSIBLE on slower or remote links, not shown here.
findings.fix: Make the known gap exact: the save can precede a write only while the room socket is under backpressure; while another cell streams, the write then waits for nh's next write or run end; and the calling tool can wait on the drain. Optionally make the ordering robust: before sending, wait until the websocket is not paused plus a loop step, and bound the send with `asyncio.wait_for(..., a few s)` so a tool call never waits on the drain. Optionally add a unit test that the request comes after the queued update.

findings.issue: One of the five call sites the side doc lists, `_reset_stuck`'s `await doc.save()` (line 299), is covered by no test. Reverting it to `settle()` passes the save unit tests and the stuck-cell integration tests.
findings.evidence: Scratch mutant c12b/review-gateway/m6 (line 299 `await doc.save()` -> `await doc.settle()`): `pytest tests/unit/test_rtc_save.py` 5 passed; `pytest -m integration tests/integration/test_backend_review.py tests/integration/test_rtc_document.py -k 'stuck or running'` 3 passed.
findings.fix: In test_rtc_save.py, drive `_reset_stuck` with a WriteDoc-style fake (stuck_cells returns an id, `_session_busy` False, end_run recorded) and assert 'end_run' is followed by 'save'.

findings.issue: `validate_utf8` is not exactly equivalent to websocket-client's check. It returns False for a valid prefix cut at the end, where websocket-client's DFA returns True. On text frames the net result is identical, because `WebSocketApp` decodes afterwards (only the exception type and message change). On close frames it differs: `ABNF.validate` also calls it on the close reason, and websocket-client decodes that reason inside `try/except UnicodeDecodeError`. A close frame whose reason ends mid-sequence was accepted before and is now 'Invalid close frame.' (an error instead of a clean close). The kernel.py docstring and side doc line 84 say it 'refuses what websocket-client refused'. It refuses a superset. Practically unreachable (Tornado sends whole UTF-8 reasons), but the claim is inexact.
findings.evidence: Fuzz (c12b/review-gateway/fuzz_utf8.py, 5,477,952 inputs: every 1- and 2-byte string, every 3-byte string with a lead byte >= 0xC0, 4-byte strings with leads F0-F7 plus continuation and edge bytes, 200k random, cut, flipped and spliced strings, and str/bytearray/memoryview): 141,751 raw differences, all of kind (nh False, websocket-client True, cut-at-end True); 0 differences in 'refused by the check or WebSocketApp's decode'. Close frame `struct.pack('!H',1000)+b'bye \xe2\x82'` through `ABNF.validate(False)`: upstream 'accepted', with nh's check 'WebSocketProtocolException: Invalid close frame.'
findings.fix: Either make the text exact ('refuses what websocket-client refused on text frames; additionally refuses a close reason cut mid-sequence, which RFC 6455 forbids'), or keep websocket-client's close-frame behaviour: patch only the name `continuous_frame.extract` sees, or accept a cut end the way the DFA does. The fuzz result supports the text-frame claim as is.

findings.issue: The dedicated pin `'validate_utf8' in continuous_frame.extract.__code__.co_names` doesn't prove the reader calls the patched global. co_names also holds attribute names, so an upstream refactor to `_utils.validate_utf8(frame.data)` keeps it green while nh's patch no longer runs. Today the refactor is caught only incidentally: the parametrized cut case `b'\xe2\x82'` in `test_invalid_text_frames_are_refused_as_before` fails, because nh differs from upstream on that one input. If upstream also starts rejecting a cut end, no unit test would notice.
findings.evidence: I replaced `continuous_frame.extract` with a copy that calls `_utils.validate_utf8(...)`. Result: 'pin 1 (attr is nh's): True', 'pin 2 (name in co_names): True', b'\xff' refused, b'\xe2\x82' accepted (so only the parametrized case fails).
findings.fix: Pin by behaviour: monkeypatch `websocket._abnf.validate_utf8` with a sentinel that records calls, run `text_frame(b'x')` through `continuous_frame.extract`, and assert the sentinel was called.

findings.issue: The private-attribute patch is unguarded and has no version check. `import websocket._abnf` at module top (line 23) makes a renamed or removed private module an ImportError that stops the whole gateway from importing, not just the speed-up. If the attribute is renamed, line 48 silently adds a new attribute and the fix quietly stops working. A changed call signature would raise TypeError on every text frame. The drift job, the one place a newer websocket-client runs, doesn't run the unit pins: drift.yml line 31 runs `tests/contract tests/gateway tests/unit/test_fake_backend.py`, not tests/unit/test_kernel_utf8.py or tests/unit/test_rtc_save.py. So a rename would show there only as an a7 timing-budget failure. Installs are `uv sync --frozen` (nh-sync line 138), so users are safe until the lock is bumped.
findings.evidence: kernel.py:23 `import websocket._abnf`; kernel.py:48 `websocket._abnf.validate_utf8 = validate_utf8  # type: ignore[attr-defined]` with no check that it replaces `websocket._utils.validate_utf8`. drift.yml:31 as quoted. The test file's own docstring says: 'Against websocket-client's latest release (the drift job), a7's receive budget ... is what fails if it doesn't.'
findings.fix: Patch only if `getattr(websocket._abnf, 'validate_utf8', None) is websocket._utils.validate_utf8`, inside try/except (ImportError, AttributeError), and log once at warning otherwise, so the gateway still starts, only slower. Add tests/unit/test_kernel_utf8.py and tests/unit/test_rtc_save.py to drift.yml's upstream-latest pytest line, so an upstream rename fails with a named test rather than a timing budget.

findings.issue: `_on_message` drops every RAW message (rtc.py:89), including save replies with status 'failed' (the server couldn't save) or 'skipped' (an out-of-band reload held the lock). A save that never happened leaves no trace in gateway.log, so an a8-type loss can't be diagnosed afterwards.
findings.evidence: jupyter_server_ydoc/handlers.py on_message answers `{"type": "save", "responseTo": id, "status": "success"|"skipped"|"failed"}` as RAW. rtc.py:89 `if message and message[0] == RAW_MESSAGE: return` without reading it.
findings.fix: Decode the reply (pycrdt Decoder: read_var_uint, then read_var_string, then json) and `log.info` when a save reply's status is not 'success'. Keep ignoring everything else.

findings.issue: Pre-existing, outside the delta, found while testing the save: jupyter-nbmodel-client's listener busy-loops at 100% CPU and freezes the gateway's event loop when the room server closes nh's room websocket cleanly (close codes 1000/1001/1005, e.g. a proxy sending 'going away'). `_listen_to_websocket` is `while True: async for message in websocket`. websockets' `__aiter__` returns on ConnectionClosedOK, and the next `recv()` raises again at once without yielding. NhNbModelClient (rtc.py) doesn't guard against it. Not triggered by a8: there the server is SIGKILLed, which gives 1006 (ConnectionClosedError, run() ends).
findings.evidence: order_demo.py: a local websockets room server whose handler returned (a clean 1000 close). The gateway process then sat at ~91% CPU and never finished `await asyncio.sleep(5.5)`. faulthandler showed the loop stuck in websockets/asyncio/connection.py:317 recv <- :237 __aiter__ <- jupyter_nbmodel_client/client.py:100 _listen_to_websocket. websockets/frames.py OK_CLOSE_CODES = {1000, 1001, 1005}.
findings.fix: Out of this chunk's scope: queue it separately. For example, NhNbModelClient could override run(), or wrap its `_on_message` partial, so that a clean close ends run() and the next write reconnects. Or report it upstream.

reviews.checked:
Room save protocol, matched against the installed code:
- nh's `save_message` is varuint 2, varstring "save", varuint id, with ids from 1.
- JupyterLab's own client sends the same bytes: the docprovider-extension bundle does `++this._saveCounter`, then `w.zd(o,2), w.Qj(o,"save"), w.zd(o,e)`.
- jupyter_server_ydoc 3.0.4 handlers.py decodes those bytes with Decoder and saves at once through `_save_to_disc` (save_now=True).
- I downloaded jupyter-server-ydoc 3.0.0-3.0.3 from PyPI: their `_save_to_disc`, `_maybe_save_document` and on_message are identical. nh's gate (jupyter-collaboration >=5,<6) therefore gets the same protocol throughout.

Room save runtime behaviour:
- It is sent only while synced (`RtcDocument.save` checks `synced`; `request_save` needs a websocket).
- It never raises into a write; the send runs on the loop, next to nbmodel's own direct sends.
- Tornado awaits `on_message`'s save before reading nh's next frame: the documented cost, confirmed in tornado/websocket.py:1216-1218.
- nh's awareness has no `autosave` field, so the room already treated autosave as on (true, pre-existing).
- nh's save goes through the same `_maybe_save_document` as autosave, so it adds no new dialog path. I did not check this in a browser.
- The `_run_done` closure captures the right `doc`; `_saves` keeps the tasks alive.

Room save tests:
- A scratch mutant with every save removed (c12b/review-gateway/m1) fails all three a8 tests (8 cells expected, 3 on disk) and the root-cause test alone (not on disk within 5 s). The unmodified copy passes.
- A mutant with the settle() before the request removed (m4) fails all three a8 tests.
- The pre-existing Lab non-exit on SIGTERM happens with and without the fix (the server had not exited after 25 s in both).
- a8 alone, twice: 3 passed each time (39.6 s). No jupyter or ipykernel process left afterwards, nor after my other Lab runs.

UTF-8 check:
- Fuzzed against websocket-client's DFA on 5.48M inputs (results in GW-4).
- bytearray, memoryview and str behave like websocket-client's.
- Speed: 10.1 MB in 26 ms versus 198 ms per MB for the DFA.
- The patch is installed once at import, before any client thread starts.
- kernel.py is not in lint.py's import chain.
- The unit tests pass (31 targeted tests, together with the prune ones).

Prune keep=:
- Kept files sort first, count toward the caps and are never deleted.
- `shape_outputs` passes the basenames of the originals and the full copy it just wrote.
- A mutant without keep= (m5) fails `test_a_call_s_own_copies_survive_its_prune`.
- The design §3.2 and §6.8 lines on prune match the code.

Workflows: actionlint passes on both drift.yml and ci.yml.

The worktree is unchanged: git status is as before, and there is no hooks __pycache__. All scratch work is under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Notebook-Harness-Plugin/7418c2d8-0b1e-58d2-873f-2c6f1cdc8600/scratchpad/c12b/review-gateway/ (fuzz_utf8.py, order_demo*.py, test_nosave_probe.py, mutants m1/m4/m5/m6, copies p-*/x-*).

findings.issue: A secret found by a pattern and longer than the trim margin (17,408 chars) can leak if it starts before the tail window's raw start. `_clean_share` (lines 407-412) drops only the first `margin` cleaned chars of the tail window. The unbounded patterns (token=/secret=/key= `_VALUE`, quoted `_WORD`, the password/secret phrase, Authorization Bearer/Basic, and the ghp_/sk-/xox tails) need their literal to recognise the value. That literal is left of the window, so the rest of the value past the margin is kept unredacted. design.md:1061 lists this as a Known gap, but the Trim block at design.md:1022 says 'So the kept text holds no secret, and no piece of one, that redacting the whole text would have caught', which is false. Graded blocker because the lens counts every leak as one. The trigger is one token or phrase over 17 KB, such as a large JWT or a base64 blob after token=/secret=/Bearer.
findings.evidence: Scratch script c12b/review-redaction/demo_long.py uses the real Redactor.for_project with a .env and TRIM_CHARS patched to 200,000 (the margin stays the real 17,408). It builds one 400,000-char stream and places the secret's literal 5,000 chars before the tail window's raw start (266,963), with a 40,000-char value. HEAD 17ae694's whole-text shape_outputs shows 0 chars of the value in each case. The trimmed full copy holds about 17,500 chars of it: 'Authorization: Bearer <40k>' gives 17,536 of 40,000; '{"access_token": "<40k>"}' gives 17,536; 'ghp_'+40k gives 17,472; 'password = "<40k>"' gives 17,536. With max_chars=200,000 the result also held runs of 4,096 or more consecutive chars of it.
findings.fix: Stop a kept tail from starting inside a value run that began before the cut. Two ways: (a) grow the tail window left, bounded, to the start of its first line or first delimiter, then redact; or (b) move the tail's start past the end of the run the cut falls in. For (b): at the first line break, which ends every pattern value; with no line break, at the first whitespace or quote, which ends every value except a quoted password/secret phrase, and that ends at its closing quote or line end. At minimum, correct design.md:1022 so it does not contradict the gap at design.md:1061. Add a test with a Bearer token longer than the margin that starts before the tail window.

findings.issue:
HTML over its trim share leaks pieces of secrets. `_clean_texts` (line 378) calls `_html_to_text(raw, share)`. That redacts the markup with `redact_head`, cuts it at the share, parses it and then runs `_clean`. Some secrets are whole only in the parsed text and not in the markup: split by or inline tags, broken by whitespace the parser collapses, or written as entities that `_with_encoded` does not produce (numeric entities, markupsafe's '/"). For these, the part before the cut survives `_clean`. It is followed by '\n[… HTML cut …]', not '...' or the end of the text, so fragment matching does not fire, and a pattern needs its full length. Separately, `redact_head` uses the redactor's margin (1024) and stops once its redacted window is long enough in total. Markers longer than the values they replace can therefore hide a private key cut open at the window edge. Both problems exist at HEAD's 1 MB cut (same code). The trim now reaches them for any HTML, even under 1 MB, in a call over TRIM_CHARS. The unit test test_html_is_cut_at_its_share_after_redaction only plants a plain value inside

.
findings.evidence: c12b/review-redaction/demo_html4.py: TRIM_CHARS=1,500,000; outputs are a 600k stream, 700k HTML (planned share 500,000) and a 600k stream. The secret is split by <wbr> every 8 chars and the cut is swept across it. The full copy shows 28 of 29 chars of the .env value ('Sup3rS3cret-Passw0rd-2026-xY') and 'ghp_'+19 chars of a GitHub token ('ghp_pLIix6MEOLeMa61EqJo'). HEAD shows neither: that HTML is under 1 MB and is not cut. demo_html3b.py shows the same through `_html_to_text(markup, 1000)` + `_clean`. demo_html2.py puts 700 table rows 'postgresql://uN:pN@dbN' before a 12,411-char RSA key whose END line is 1,500 chars past a 300,000 cut. Result: 12 of 190 body lines (768 chars) in the cleaned text, against 0 in the whole text.
findings.fix: When HTML is cut: redact and parse a markup window of limit + `_trim_margin()`, run `_clean` on the text, then drop the text's last margin chars before appending '[… HTML cut …]'. Tags and entities only shrink text, so any piece that the window edge or the cut leaves sits in those chars; an unterminated key body left unredacted is at most about 8.2K. Add tests for a <wbr>-split value and token and for a key over 9 KB at the HTML cut.

findings.issue: An error over its trim share has its frames joined with '\n' and cleaned as one text (`_error_info`, lines 689-695), even when the frames themselves fit their share. Untrimmed, each frame is cleaned alone, so a frame's end is 'the end of the text' for the redactor's fragment rule (a secret-named value's 12+ char head piece right before the end is redacted). Joined, a middle frame's end is followed by '\n', so that piece is no longer redacted. Graded blocker because the lens counts every leak as one; in practice it needs a frame that ends in an unmarked cut piece of a secret-named value.
findings.evidence: c12b/review-redaction/frames.py uses DB_PASSWORD from .env. Its first 16 chars end the middle one of three frames. With evalue 'bad password' (12 chars), the piece is in none of the result, the full copy or error.traceback. With evalue 'bad password '+9,000,000 chars (error over the cap, frames small enough to fit whole), the piece is in the result, the full copy and error.traceback (True, True, True).
findings.fix: When the joined frames fit their share, clean each frame alone, as the untrimmed branch does. When they must be trimmed, give frames their own shares (water-fill per frame) or trim per frame, so frame ends stay text ends. Add a test with a piece at the end of a middle frame under a huge evalue.

findings.issue: Progress-bar output over the cap loses everything, including its last line. `_clean_share` measures the margin it drops in cleaned chars. A head window (about 2.4M raw) or tail window (about 5.6M raw) of \r-rewritten output collapses under `terminal_text` to a few KB, under 17,408. Both `head` and `tail` then come out empty, and the result and the full copy are only '[… N chars cut …]'. Before the trim the same output showed its final state. So design.md:1012's 'The head keeps 30% and the tail 70% of share − 2 × margin' does not hold. Not a leak; a functional regression on a common kind of large output (training loops that print with end='\r', Keras-style progress bars).
findings.evidence:
c12b/review-redaction/progress.py uses the real TRIM_CHARS and 400,000 writes of 'step i/400000 loss …', then '
final accuracy 0.9731
' (13,600,023 chars). Trim result: '[stdout]

[… 13,600,022 chars cut …]

[full output: …]', and the copy holds only the marker. HEAD result: 'step  399999/400000 loss 0.000003
final accuracy 0.9731'. keras_like.py: 200 epochs × 700 '' updates, 9,246,692 raw chars, 19,691 cleaned. Trim result: 84 chars, the marker '9,246,691 chars cut' and the footer. HEAD: the last epochs with val_loss. counts.py with TRIM 200k and tqdm-style bars: kept 0.
findings.fix: Grow a window, like `redact_head` does, until its cleaned form reaches its target plus the margin (bounded by the text). Or translate the raw margin into cleaned coordinates. For the tail there is a narrower option: if the tail window's first line has a '\r' (not part of '\r\n') after the raw edge, that line needs no margin drop, since collapse starts it after its last '\r'. Add a test with a \r progress loop over the cap that checks the final line is kept.

findings.issue: The §6.8 Trim block overstates what the code does. Line 1022's 'no secret, and no piece of one' is contradicted by R1 to R3, and R1 is even listed as a known gap at line 1061. Line 1012's 30%/70% keep is false under R4. Line 1015 presents the HTML cut as safe 'as before' (R2). Line 1007 says a call cleans 'at most TRIM_CHARS raw characters'. But `redact_head` keeps doubling its window past that on markup that redaction shrinks, and summarize_outputs cleans ename whole. The Counts bullet (line 1023) says N moves 'by a few chars'. That holds for colour codes inside the kept pieces, but trimmed markers count raw chars while untrimmed ones count cleaned chars, so N changes unit at the cap. On \r or ANSI-heavy output this is large. Separately, docs/harness-toml.md:105 still says 'The full text is saved under `.nh/outputs/`'; past TRIM_CHARS the copy holds only the head and tail. The scope allows correcting this line.
findings.evidence: c12b/review-redaction/html_bound.py: a 40,760,015-char HTML table of a 1,001-char .env value, planned as 1,000,000. The redactor scanned 63,628,628 chars in 7 calls, against TRIM_CHARS 8,000,000. counts.py: coloured lines give marker N 1,627,358, while the cleaned whole minus kept is 607,358. keras_like.py: '9,246,691 chars cut' for a text that is 19,691 chars cleaned. `grep -n 'outputs/' docs/harness-toml.md` gives line 105 with the old wording.
findings.fix: After fixing R1 to R4, restate the Trim block's guarantees and Known gaps to match: the HTML path, frames, and the unit of N for \r/ANSI output. State the real bound, or bound `redact_head` in the HTML trim path. Change harness-toml.md:105 to say that past TRIM_CHARS the copy keeps each long text's head and tail with a '[… N chars cut …]' line.

findings.issue: Two private-key gaps that predate this chunk (C3); the trim does not cause them. The lens asked for a key over 16 KiB. (1) The END line is looked for only within PEM_MAX_CHARS (16,384) of the body. A longer key is treated as unterminated and only 8,192 body chars are redacted, so the rest shows even with no trim at all. Known Gaps does not list this. (2) A CSI escape that is open right before the key ('\x1b[3-----BEGIN') is removed by terminal_text's CSI regex as '\x1b[3-----B'. The BEGIN line is then no longer seen and the whole key shows. This needs malformed output.
findings.evidence: c12b/review-redaction/pem_big.py: a 19,561-char RSA key between two lines, through HEAD 17ae694's shape_outputs with no cut, shows 173 of 300 body lines. pem_pre.py: with a fill whose ANSI codes are cut open next to the key, HEAD's whole-text shaping leaks 52/512 (12 KB key) and 70/676 (16 KB key) placements, each preceded by ' . \x1b[3-----BEGIN R'. The same placements leak 0 times with fills that have no escapes.
findings.fix: Outside this chunk: open a separate task to redact the body of an unterminated key up to the end of its base64 run (or document it as a Known gap), and to check for BEGIN before stripping, or keep dashes out of CSI intermediates for the redactor's view.
